requirement_mappings.note: The scenario first delivers a matching regional interaction, unsubscribes the exact non-empty region set from that interaction class, then sends again and asserts that the callback count does not increase. This directly tests removal of the specified region from that class's subscription region set; it does not test multi-region partial removal.

After subscribing to one region, the scenario requests unsubscription of a different, committed non-empty region that was never in the interaction class's subscription set, then verifies a send overlapping the original region still produces the expected callback. With a non-empty region active in the subscription set, the scenario calls Unsubscribe Interaction Class With Regions using an empty set and verifies that a matching send is still delivered. This directly tests that the empty set removes no subscription.

After deleting a committed region that was never subscribed, the scenario passes its retained handle to Unsubscribe Interaction Class With Regions and requires InvalidRegion. It then verifies the active subscription still delivers. This directly tests a deleted designator on this service only, not foreign-region or invalid-context handling.

The Requirements Lab candidate currently exports this service to §10.24.6; the official RTIambassador.h places Get Dimension Upper Bound at §10.25, and RL-442 records that known crosswalk defect. No Lab resynchronization or mapping change is made here.

Both successful and InvalidDimensionHandle reports check the supplied Dimension handle argument record uses Table 5 type code 10 and the standard argument name. The Java failure handle is produced by the official API in a separate FOM execution; provider-specific handle text is checked only for quoted shape.
The InvalidDimensionHandle report checks the no-return value as the Table 5 Null form: type code 34, empty name, and null value.

scenarios.mapping_note: Direct mappings remain limited to the positive GetDimensionUpperBound return in IEEE 1516.1-2025 §10.25 (with known RL-442 crosswalk defect) and the two Table 5 argument/return forms in §11.5.1. The Java success path checks bound 64. Its failure path uses TckAdditionalDimension from a separately created federation because the Java API has no default-invalid DimensionHandle; it checks the InvalidDimensionHandle service result, quoted handle shape, Null return, and invoking federate. This does not claim other dimension errors, every service-report form, or complete §10.25 coverage.
